title: Call Stack Peak Memory
description:
You are given a valid trace of stack-frame memory `events` executed by a single-threaded program:
- `"CALL <bytes>"`: pushes a new stack frame initialized with `<bytes>` bytes.
- `"ALLOC <bytes>"`: allocates `<bytes>` additional bytes owned by the currently active (top) stack frame.
- `"SHRINK <bytes>"`: frees `min(topFrameBytes, <bytes>)` bytes from the currently active stack frame.
- `"RET"`: pops the currently active stack frame, immediately releasing all bytes owned by that frame.

Return the **peak total memory** (in bytes, as a 64-bit integer `long`) held across all active stack frames at any point during execution.
constraints: Every byte value is a non-negative integer <= 10^9.
ALLOC, SHRINK, and RET are only called when at least one frame is active.
hints: Maintain a stack storing the current memory owned by each active frame alongside a running total `curMem` and `peakMem`.
On `SHRINK b`, compute `freed = min(stack[-1], b)` to update both the top frame and `curMem`; on `RET`, pop the top frame and subtract its full memory from `curMem`.

examples.explanation: CALL 100 -> 100, CALL 50 -> 150, ALLOC 80 -> 230 (peak), RET frees 130 -> 100, RET -> 0.
CALL 10 -> 10, SHRINK 25 reduces frame to 0 -> 0, ALLOC 40 -> 40 (peak), RET -> 0.
First call reaches 70 and returns; second call reaches 90 (peak).
